description: GROUP BY ALL groups by every NON-AGGREGATE select item without naming them. An expression item groups just as a bare column does, so SELECT LOWER(region), COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY ALL groups by the folded value. When EVERY item is an aggregate there is nothing to group by, and the result is one grand-total row. It composes with HAVING and with joins, taking its keys from both sides. Converted 1:1 from query/GroupByAllTest (now retired); the Java read individual row indexes, which the converted tests state as whole ordered row sets.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
SELECT region, city, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY region, city
CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
SELECT LOWER(region), COUNT(*) FROM sales GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1
CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
SELECT SUM(amount), COUNT(*) FROM sales GROUP BY ALL
CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, amount INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE regions (region VARCHAR, mgr VARCHAR)
SELECT r.mgr, s.region, SUM(s.amount) AS total FROM sales s JOIN regions r ON r.region = s.region GROUP BY ALL HAVING SUM(s.amount) > 30 ORDER BY r.mgr
